elements.quote: ► A significant number of people continue to describe ongoing symptoms long after the acute phase of COVID‐19, often referred to as long COVID. ► Long COVID is a heterogeneous condition with an uncertain prevalence, for which there is currently no precise case definition.
elements.reason: Directly describes the current state of knowledge and important uncertainties about long COVID.

elements.quote: This study aims to regularly synthesise evidence on long COVID characteristics, to help inform clinical management, rehabilitation strategies and interventional studies to improve long‐term outcomes.
elements.reason: Explains the importance and need for the review by stating its purpose in informing practice and research.

elements.quote: Systematic reviews conducted early during the COVID‐19 pandemic soon became redundant due to the rapidity with which new research was released. We conducted a 'living' systematic review to provide frequently updated evidence on the symptoms and complications of long COVID.
elements.reason: The need for the current review is explained due to redundancy of early reviews, but no specific previous review is identified or cited.
The review is not focused on intervention effects; it is a descriptive review of long COVID characteristics.
The review does not involve complex interventions or delivery contexts; it is a descriptive synthesis.

elements.quote: Peer-­ reviewed studies were considered eligible if they included at least 100 people with laboratory confirmed and/or clinically diagnosed COVID-­ 19. Without a clear, internationally agreed case definition, we included studies that reported symptoms or outcomes assessed at 12 or more weeks post COVID-­ 19 onset. Reviews and opinion pieces were excluded. Studies were excluded if they included fewer than 100 participants, to avoid small study effects, 18 or the follow-­ up was unclear or less than 12 weeks post onset.
elements.reason: Study designs, population size, diagnosis, and follow-up requirements are specified, but settings are not explicitly stated as eligibility criteria.

elements.quote: Peer-­ reviewed studies were considered eligible. There were no language restrictions. Data extraction was not performed for non-­ peer-­ reviewed preprints.
elements.reason: Language and publication status are specified, but dissemination year is not explicitly stated in eligibility criteria.
No evidence found distinguishing exclusion due to outcomes not measured versus not reported.

elements.quote: We presented symptom proportions by different settings, as presented in the individual studies: hospitalised, non-­ hospitalised or a mix of both populations if no subset data were available. Symptoms were broadly grouped into physiological clusters through discussion with clinicians.
elements.reason: Groups for synthesis (by settings and symptom clusters) are specified and linked to the review's objective of characterizing long COVID symptoms.

elements.quote: Across studies, 37% (95% CI 18.43 to 59.93) of patients reported reduced quality of life. Although high I² values (>80%) were observed... We also performed subgroup analysis based on setting (hospitalised vs non-hospitalised) and follow-up time. In several symptoms and signs, the heterogeneity of the results was found to be associated with level of hospitalisation, hospital settings, location of the studies and follow-up timing using subgroup analysis (online supplemental files 5-8). Using meta-regression, the proportion of female patients in the studies was positively associated with headache and smell and taste disturbance (online supplemental file 9), while the proportion of ICU patients in the studies was positively associated with muscle pain (online supplemental file 10). No major difference was found in the sensitivity analyses (online supplemental files 11 and 12). Asymmetries found in the funnel plots suggest reporting biases and poor methodological quality in the included studies (online supplemental file 13).
elements.reason: Reports results of meta-analysis with estimate and precision, heterogeneity measures, subgroup analysis, meta-regression, sensitivity analyses, and funnel plots, referencing supplemental files for details.
